source.title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions

accepted.question_text: Let (K_i)_{i\ge 1} be compact subsets of ℝ such that 0\in K_i for every i, every element of every K_i is nonnegative, \operatorname{diam}(K_i)>0 for all i, and \operatorname{diam}(K_i)	o 0. Define S={∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j\mid x_j\in K_j} and, for each z, define the tail set R_z={∑_{i=z+1}^∞ x_i\mid x_i\in K_i}. What topological spaces can S be homeomorphic to?

evidence.quote:
Instead, we list the following open questions:
1. What are the possible sets S can be homeomorphic to?

accepted.question_text: In the same setting where S={∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j\mid x_j\in K_j} for compact sets K_i\subseteq ℝ with 0\in K_i and \operatorname{diam}(K_i)	o 0, and where R_z={∑_{i=z+1}^∞ x_i\mid x_i\in K_i} denotes the tail set, what conditions on the tails R_z guarantee that S is an interval or a finite union of intervals?

evidence.quote:
2. Under what conditions on the tail Rz will this set be an interval or a finite
union of intervals?

accepted.question_text: In the same real compact-set sumset setting, what conditions on the tail sets R_z guarantee that S is an M-Cantorval (a perfect set whose every gap is accumulated on both sides by infinitely many intervals and gaps), an L-Cantorval (every gap has an interval adjacent on the right and is accumulated on the left by infinitely many intervals and gaps), or an R-Cantorval (the left-right reversed version)?

evidence.quote:
3. Under what conditions on the tail Rz will this set be an M-Cantorval? An
L or R Cantorval?

accepted.question_text: Let α_i and λ_i be null sequences with α_i → 0 and λ_i → 0, and for each i let K_i be the middle-α_i Cantor set whose first construction interval is [0, λ_i]. If S is the sumset formed from these K_i and R_z denotes the corresponding tail set, under what conditions on R_z and on the parameters α_i is S a Cantor set, and what kind of Cantor set can occur?
accepted.context_brief: Infinite sums of middle-α Cantor sets

evidence.quote:

evidence.quote:
Now we pose the following questions, inspired from the results regarding complex
radix expansions and the sets they form:

1. Under what conditions on Ki and Rz will S = C?

accepted.question_text: Let (K_i)_{i\ge 1} be compact subsets of ℂ with 0\in K_i for every i and \operatorname{diam}(K_i)	o 0, and define S={∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j\mid x_j\in K_j} with tails R_z. Under what conditions on K_i and R_z does S have fractal structure, and what is the Hausdorff dimension of S in those cases?
accepted.context_brief: Fractal geometry in the complex-plane setting

evidence.quote:
2. Several authors have investigated the fractal structures of radix represen￾tations using a complex base [15]. Under what conditions on Ki and Rz
will S have fractal structure? What will the Haussdorf dimension of S be?

accepted.question_text: Let (K_i)_{i\ge 1} be compact subsets of ℂ with 0\in K_i for every i and \operatorname{diam}(K_i)	o 0, and define S={∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j\mid x_j\in K_j} with tails R_z. Excluding the trivial case, what specific conditions on K_i and R_z guarantee that every algebraic number admits a radix-style representation arising from this sumset construction?

evidence.quote:
3. Motivated by results in algebra concerning representations in algebraic
number fields [2], besides the trivial case, what specific conditions on Ki
and Rz will we able to have a radix representation of all algebraic numbers?
